task.description: Independently validate CODE-DESIGNER's design at lib/letflow/design/iss-0048-sandbox-pool-owner-crash-reclaim.md against its own handoff's five acceptance criteria (handoffs/WF03-ISS0048-20260818/step-02-code-designer.json's task.acceptance_criteria) and against ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis (step-01). Re-derive your own verdict from the artefact and the current lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex / lib/letflow/definitions.ex source -- do NOT accept CODE-DESIGNER's own self-report as evidence. Specifically re-check: (1) the design contains no implementation code, only interfaces/@specs/pseudocode-shape; (2) it covers exactly the SandboxPool crash/kill gap and does not touch the 5 exonerated identity/role_registry test files; (3) claim/2 and release/2's public @specs are genuinely unchanged, verified against the current source, not just claimed; (4) the owner-monitor mechanism (vs. a periodic reaper) is actually justified by SandboxPool's real existing architecture -- read the module yourself and confirm the claimed Process.monitor/:DOWN precedent for waiters genuinely exists as described; (5) the design's claim that apply_promotion_assertion_rerun/6's contract is unaffected holds up against the actual call site in lib/letflow/definitions.ex.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the five acceptance criteria from step-02 is independently re-checked against the artefact/source, not copied from CODE-DESIGNER's self-report
Verdict is PASS only if all five hold; otherwise FAIL with the specific criterion/criteria that don't, routed back to CODE-DESIGNER as rework

result.summary: Independently re-derived verdict by reading lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex (276 lines, full) and lib/letflow/definitions.ex (moduledoc lines 52-77, apply_promotion_assertion_rerun/6 @doc 755-786, claim_sandbox_and_proceed/8 1472-1515, run_replay_span/8 1522-1572, handle_fixture_load_failure/7, safe_release/2) against the design artefact, not from CODE-DESIGNER's self-report. All 5 acceptance criteria hold: (1) No implementation code -- every fenced block in the design (lines 169-353) is either a @spec/type-shape or a CASE/OF/END pseudocode dispatch; no .ex def/defp body is proposed anywhere. (2) Scope is exactly SandboxPool's crash/kill gap -- SS1 scope table and SS8 'what ELIXIR-DEV must NOT change' both confine every change to lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex; no reference anywhere to editing identity_test.exs/user_test.exs/group_test.exs/tenant_role_test.exs/role_registry_test.exs. (3) claim/2 and release/2's @specs in design SS4 are byte-for-byte identical to the live source (sandbox_pool.ex:86-94 and :100-106) -- verified by direct text comparison, not assumed. (4) The owner-monitor precedent is real, not invented: sandbox_pool.ex:186-191 (handle_queue_or_reject/3) does call Process.monitor(caller_pid) for waiting callers today, and handle_info({:DOWN, caller_ref, :process, _pid, _reason}, state) already exists at sandbox_pool.ex:155-164 -- confirmed by direct read, matching the design's SS2.1 claim exactly; the reaper-rejection reasoning in SS2.2 is substantively correct (req039's in-memory-GenServer rationale, sandbox_* schemas deliberately excluded from tenant_schemas) though its point 2 misattributes that tenant_schemas exclusion to a comment at 'sandbox_pool.ex:239-243' when the actual statement is in the moduledoc at lines 9-11 (239-243 is CREATE SCHEMA/injection-safety commentary with no tenant_schemas mention) -- a minor line-citation slip, not a false claim, since the substance is confirmed true elsewhere in the same file. (5) SS7's claim that apply_promotion_assertion_rerun/6's contract is unaffected holds up: claim_sandbox_and_proceed/8 (definitions.ex:1472) calls SandboxPool.claim/2 synchronously with no Task.async/spawn anywhere in its body or run_replay_span/8's, confirming the design's load-bearing premise that claim/2's caller pid IS the process ISSUE-FIXER's kill scenario targets; run_replay_span/8's try/rescue (1532-1571) wraps Steps 3-6 and calls safe_release/2 -> SandboxPool.release/2 only on a raised exception, never on an exit signal (the process is gone before rescue could run), so the two safety nets are correctly described as non-overlapping/layered with no double-release race. No FAIL-worthy gap found in any of the 5 criteria.
